note: Decision portal. These are the questions that must be answered before a decision can be made, the information we have vs. do not have, and the suggestions for discovering what is missing. Nothing here is a claim about popularity, search volume or product superiority.

open_questions.question: Do we keep the submitted link.amazon short links, or replace them with tagged Special Links generated in the Associates console?
open_questions.what_we_know: All five submitted links resolve to real Amazon listings. Each submitted token is a 9-character short-link token, not a 10-character ASIN. Program Policies 6(w) prohibits using link shortening in a way that makes the Amazon destination unclear. The exact compliance status of the supplied short links is unresolved.
open_questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether the enrolled Associates account exists and can generate tagged Special Links for these five ASINs; Amazon's specific determination of these short links.

options.label: Replace with tagged Special Links
options.tradeoff: Most compliant and trackable; requires an enrolled Associates account and a one-link-per-product test in the enrolled workflow.

options.label: Keep short links with explicit Amazon disclosure
options.tradeoff: Fastest; carries unresolved 6(w) risk and weaker tracking.

options.label: Hybrid (short links now, Special Links at scale)
options.tradeoff: Ship immediately, de-risk later; two link formats to manage.

open_questions.recommendation: Replace with tagged Special Links before scaling. Test one link per product in the enrolled Associates workflow and confirm the destination and tracking report before scaling.
open_questions.how_to_discover: Log into Associates Central, generate a Special Link for each resolved ASIN, and open each once to confirm the destination and that the click appears in the tracking report.

open_questions.question: How do we display star ratings and review counts for the products whose ratings we could not capture?
open_questions.what_we_know: ThermoMaven's rating was captured from the official listing (4.6 stars, 3,499 ratings). The other four ratings are displayed on their listings but were not captured in this extraction. Program Policies 6(t) restricts displaying Amazon customer reviews or star ratings unless obtained via Creators API or PA API.
open_questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether the account has Creators/PA API access; the exact numeric ratings for the four products.

options.label: Show rating only where captured; blank + flag the rest
options.tradeoff: Fully honest; the comparison table looks uneven.

options.label: Point the rating cell to the listing ('see listing')
options.tradeoff: Reader can verify; not a stored value.

options.label: Pull ratings via Creators/PA API
options.tradeoff: Compliant and complete; requires API access and compliance with the License.

open_questions.recommendation: Show the captured rating and leave the four uncaptured ratings blank with a flag. Do not infer values.
open_questions.how_to_discover: Request Creators/PA API access through Associates Central and pull ratings through the official API if granted.

open_questions.question: How do we display prices under the Program Policies price-display rule?
open_questions.what_we_know: Buy-box prices were read from each official listing on 2026-11-19. Program Policies 2(b) states prices and availability may only be shown if (a) Amazon serves the link with that price data, or (b) the data is obtained via Creators API or PA API.
open_questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether the links we publish will be Amazon-served price links or static; API access status.

options.label: Show 'as listed' price with a live listing link and a verify date
options.tradeoff: Transparent; price may drift, so a date and a link are required.

options.label: API-driven live price
options.tradeoff: Accurate and compliant; requires API access.

open_questions.recommendation: Show the price as listed, label it 'as listed on 2026-11-19', and link to the live listing so the reader sees the current price. Do not present a price comparison against non-Amazon sellers.
open_questions.how_to_discover: Confirm whether the published links will be Amazon-served price links, or obtain Creators/PA API access for live pricing.

open_questions.question: Where does the self-hosted analytics endpoint run, given GitHub Pages is static?
open_questions.what_we_know: The site is served statically from GitHub Pages, which cannot receive POST requests. The five events (page_view, cta_click, product_click, filter_apply, guide_read) are defined and the client counter is built.
open_questions.what_we_do_not_know: The chosen hosting for the collection endpoint.

options.label: Serverless function at /collect (Netlify / Vercel / Deno)
options.tradeoff: Self-hosted, privacy-preserving, no third party; needs a small deploy.

options.label: Client-only local counter
options.tradeoff: No server needed; data stays on the client and is not aggregated.

open_questions.recommendation: Deploy a small serverless /collect function alongside the static site and point the counter at it. Keep the counter cookie-free and store only an anonymous local ID.
open_questions.how_to_discover: Choose the hosting for the endpoint and confirm the privacy posture (no cookies, no cross-site tracking).

open_questions.question: What imagery do we use, given the Operating Agreement treats images as Program Content?
open_questions.what_we_know: Operating Agreement §1 treats data, images and text as Program Content. Generated or copied photography is not permitted. S-18 (real product photography) needs a decision first.
open_questions.what_we_do_not_know: Which official imagery channels are permitted for our use; whether brand press assets are usable.

options.label: Text-led, no product photos for now
Use only Amazon-served/Program Content imagery per the Agreement
Commission original product photography
options.tradeoff: Strong and original; cost and lead time.

open_questions.recommendation: Stay text-led and editorial now. Add imagery only through an officially permitted channel once confirmed.
open_questions.how_to_discover: Confirm with the Operating Agreement and Program Policies which imagery is permitted, then source accordingly.

open_questions.question: What is the publishing cadence, and which guides go first?
open_questions.what_we_know: Eight question-shaped guides are drafted. The site has a sitemap and RSS feed ready to accept each new guide.
open_questions.what_we_do_not_know: Measured query demand — we have no analytics yet, so topic priority is currently editorial.

options.label: Publish all eight now
options.tradeoff: Full library immediately; no measured prioritization.

options.label: Publish in phases, reorder by measured queries
Publish a weekly cadence with one new guide each week

open_questions.recommendation: Publish the eight guides on a weekly cadence, then reorder the next topics from measured queries in Search Console and the analytics endpoint rather than instinct.
open_questions.how_to_discover: Turn on Search Console and the analytics endpoint, then read the real query and click data after the first weeks.

suggestions.title: Put a compliance gate in front of publishing
suggestions.description: Before any guide is published, run a checklist: disclosure strip present, all outbound product links marked rel="sponsored", price labeled 'as listed' with a date, and no inferred values.
suggestions.expected_outcome: Every published page passes the same gate; no page ships non-compliant.

suggestions.title: Add a provenance table to the Research Desk
suggestions.description: Publish a dated provenance trail for every data point so any value can be traced to the official source and the date it was read.
suggestions.expected_outcome: Readers and reviewers can audit any row in one click.

suggestions.title: Add a reader-capture point (newsletter)
suggestions.description: Add a privacy-preserving email capture on the guides so returning readers can be informed of new guides.
suggestions.expected_outcome: A way to reach readers who return, without third-party tracking.

suggestions.title: Verify the site in Google Search Console
suggestions.description: Once live, submit the sitemap and verify ownership in Search Console to read real query and impression data.
suggestions.expected_outcome: Measured queries drive the next topic instead of instinct.

suggestions.title: Add FAQ and Article structured data to guides
suggestions.description: Mark up question-shaped guides with FAQPage and Article schema to improve how they present in search.
suggestions.expected_outcome: Better search presentation for question-shaped content.

suggestions.title: Add an internal site search
suggestions.description: A lightweight client-side search over the guide index so readers can jump to a question.
suggestions.expected_outcome: Lower bounce, faster path to a guide.

suggestions.title: A/B test the comparison CTA wording
suggestions.description: Once click tracking is live, test two CTA phrasings on the comparison page and pick the better from measured clicks.
suggestions.expected_outcome: Data-led CTA choice instead of guesswork.

suggestions.title: Seasonal cadence for the kitchen-appliance angle
suggestions.description: Plan dated seasonal guides (holiday cooking, spring cleaning) that tie back to the same verified products.
suggestions.expected_outcome: Relevant, dated content that can capture seasonal search.

path_chooser.label: Recommended path
path_chooser.summary: Ship the editorial site now with verified data, disclosure and rel="sponsored" in place. Replace short links with tagged Special Links as the single compliant outbound format once the Associates account confirms them. Add analytics, then let measured queries drive the next topics.
path_chooser.why: Leads with the products, keeps every dashboard surface reachable, and puts a gate in front of the parts that need a decision.

path_chooser.label: Fast path
path_chooser.summary: Publish the site with the submitted short links and a clear Amazon-destination disclosure, then swap to Special Links later.
path_chooser.why: Fastest to live, but carries the unresolved 6(w) risk and weaker tracking.

path_chooser.label: Wait-and-build path
path_chooser.summary: Hold publication until Special Links, API-driven ratings and live pricing are all in place.
path_chooser.why: Most compliant end-state, but delays having anything live to measure.
